headline: Steroids kill neurons
body: and one of them protects against it

headline: The experiment
body: Cortical neurons grown from rat brain, dosed with different androgens. | They measured mitochondrial activity, *LDH release* which means membranes are leaking, and *caspase 3/7*, the enzyme that executes apoptosis. | Testosterone, nandrolone and trenbolone all killed neurons by **apoptosis**.

headline: Trenbolone
body: reduced **neurite outgrowth**. Neurites are the extensions neurons use to connect to each other. | It downregulated *Tubb3*, the gene for the tubulin those extensions are built from. | Nandrolone hit mitochondria by 24 hours, earlier than the others.
punch: It kills cells and stops survivors wiring up.

headline: Stanozolol
body: killed by *necrosis* instead of apoptosis, and did not raise LDH the same way. | Necrosis is uncontrolled rupture, which inflames surrounding tissue.

headline: The mechanism
subhead: SECTION: NOT THE SAME FOR ALL
body: Add *flutamide* to block the androgen receptor and testosterone and nandrolone toxicity almost disappears. | So for those two it is **androgen receptor** mediated. | But methandrostenolone is different. Its toxicity is **glucocorticoid receptor** dependent and flutamide does nothing to it.
punch: Different compounds. Different receptors. Different damage.

headline: Now the part
body: that changes the picture. | *Aromatisation* and the local generation of estrogen underlie **testosterone induced neuroprotection**. | Testosterone that converts to estradiol in the brain protects neurons.
punch: Aromatisable androgens carry their own countermeasure.

headline: Which explains
body: why nandrolone and trenbolone look worse. | They are poorly aromatisable. They deliver the androgen receptor damage **without** the estrogen protection. | Nandrolone did not protect against beta amyloid toxicity the way aromatisable androgens do.
punch: Same damage. No built in defence.

headline: And this creates
body: a problem for anyone running an aromatase inhibitor alongside androgens. | You block conversion to hold the growth plate open. | You also remove the local estrogen that was protecting your neurons.
punch: Blocking aromatase removes a neuroprotective mechanism.

headline: What has been tested
body: **Exercise.** Aerobic and resistance training improved hippocampal plasticity and reversed neurocognitive changes induced by nandrolone decanoate in rats. | Physiological, biochemical and histological measures all moved. | This is a direct test against AAS neurotoxicity, not a general claim.
punch: The one intervention with a head to head result.

headline: The neurotrophics
body: *Cerebrolysin* contains peptide fragments resembling NGF, BDNF and ciliary neurotrophic factor, and is clinically used for TBI and stroke. | *9-Me-BC* inhibits MAO and raises neurotrophic factor expression in astrocytes plus tyrosine hydroxylase. | Both act on neurite outgrowth and trophic support, which is the exact thing trenbolone suppresses.
punch: Right target. No head to head trial against AAS.

headline: Others in that class
body: *Memantine* blocks excitotoxic calcium influx upstream of apoptosis. | *TAK-653* and low dose ketamine raise BDNF. | *Cortexin* and *pinealon* are short peptide preparations in the cerebrolysin family.
punch: Mechanistically aimed. Not directly tested here.

headline: So the honest ranking
body: Compound choice comes first. Aromatisable androgens carry protection that 19-nors do not. | Exercise has direct evidence against this specific damage. | Neurotrophics target the right endpoints without a head to head trial behind them.
punch: And blocking aromatase removes a defence you had.

headline: Dose and duration
body: still sit underneath all of it. | Toxicity was dose dependent, and repeated exposure was worse than single dose in every compound tested.
punch: Less, for less long, of the ones that aromatise.
